title: The fixed topic-cache model fails the five-width external gate on three new books
statement: With hyperparameters fixed from P-G-026, a normalized topic, bigram and finite-cache model beats both local-loss baselines on three previously unused historical books, but its predictive intervals contain only 4/5, 3/5 and 3/5 observed Taylor exponents. The declared joint external gate fails on all three books, so no manuscript sample was scored. Every observed exponent exceeds both empirical-bigram and token-frequency-shuffle null medians; this does not establish that the model reproduces the long-range process.
check: Find a genuinely better externally calibrated long-range model and freeze selection on separate works before evaluating additional held-back books. Retain all five widths and both local-loss baselines; validate nominal predictive coverage, unseen words, probability normalization and multiple seeds. Require the external joint gate to pass before pre-registering a suitably large separate manuscript sample, and otherwise stop without manuscript scoring. Include structured non-language alternatives and independently justified quire or sheet groups when adequate data exist.
design: Reuse the fixed P-G-026 hyperparameters (topic weight .6, cache weight .3, mean topic-switch interval 8,000; ten topics, 4,096-token cache) selected on four earlier books. Separately for each new book, fit its first 30,000 normalized tokens and score the next 30,000; no parameters are selected using these tests. Books are Villani’s Cronica, Roman de la Rose, and Chaucer’s Canterbury Tales and Other Poems. All are separate works from the hyperparameter-selection books, though these editions, languages, genres and periods do not sample all historical writing and are not independent in a population sense. Token input is standard project refcorpus normalization, ascii a–z, maximum length 30.
gate: Use exactly the earlier pilot joint gate: the candidate must have no worse test log loss than both the fixed-cache and no-cache baselines, and for each width 2,810, 4,215, 5,620, 7,025 and 8,430, the observed exponent must exceed the medians of 32 fixed-frequency shuffles and 32 test-fitted empirical-bigram samples and lie between the 4th and 61st sorted values of 64 independent model simulations. Order-statistic intervals are exploratory rather than verified nominal coverage. Work-by-width outcomes and null medians are recorded below.
normalization: The character backoff generates a first letter from a normalized 26-letter distribution, thereafter chooses either a letter or end from normalized 27-way distributions, forcing termination at length 30. The global backoff is a normalized .9 empirical-token/.1 bounded-character mixture. Each successor, topic and finite-cache component is a convex combination of an empirical distribution and this backoff, and the final distribution mixes them with nonnegative weights summing to one. The ten-state filter updates normalized weights using Bayes’ rule and a normalized state transition. This is an algebraic normalization argument for the implementation, not a separate exhaustive numerical proof of all strings. Every unseen test type has positive backoff probability; counts below include repeated unseen tokens.
limits: Parameters were optimized on the previous development works; per-book inventories, transitions and character backoff are necessarily fitted on the first 30,000 tokens of each new book. Predictive intervals and five-width joint gate are stringent exploratory checks, not formal population-coverage guarantees. Tests share widths, text samples and model fits and are dependent. Only three additional historical works were evaluated; no new structured non-language generator was fit, no reliable sheet grouping was assumed, and no manuscript data were used.

results.gate: same joint external gate as P-G-026
